ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, it is known that point $B$ is on line segment $AC$, and point $D$ is on line segment $AB$. If $BD = \frac{1}{4}AB = \frac{1}{3}CD$, with $E$ being the midpoint of line segment $AB$ and $EC=16\, \text{cm}$, find the length of line segment $AC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $BD=x$,\\
since $BD=\frac{1}{4}AB=\frac{1}{3}CD$,\\
thus $AB=4BD=4x$ and $CD=3BD=3x$,\\
therefore $BC=DC-DB=3x-x=2x$,\\
thus $AC=AB+BC=4x+2x=6x$.\\
Since $E$ is the midpoint of the segment $AB$,\\
thus $BE=\frac{1}{2}AB=\frac{1}{2}\times 4x=2x$,\\
thus $EC=BE+BC=2x+2x=4x$.\\
Furthermore, since $EC=16$,\\
thus $4x=16$,\\
solving this gives: $x=4$,\\
therefore $AC=6x=6\times 4=\boxed{24}$.
